objective_for_doctor:
Age: 31
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have left side of the chest pain, upper chest pain, and swelling in one or more areas of your body

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’m having left-sided chest pain, upper chest pain, and I also have swelling in different areas of my body—especially my right ankle and right calf, and my left tibia. I feel short of breath, I’m sweating a lot, and the pain can be a tugging/tedious kind of pain that goes to my left biceps and left scapula, and also to my shoulders. I also get worse when I lie flat (orthopnea).
[ASK] Do you have **wheezing or shortness of breath that is triggered by allergens/exposure and improves with bronchodilator-type treatment**?
No. I don’t have wheezing or allergy-triggered symptoms, and I don’t know of any improvement with bronchodilator-type treatment. My main issue is shortness of breath.
[ASK] Do you have **shortness of breath that is new or worsening**, especially with **low oxygen** or **rapid breathing**?
Yes—my shortness of breath is new and getting worse, and I’ve been breathing fast. I don’t know my oxygen level, but it feels like I’m not getting enough air.
[ASK] Do you have symptoms consistent with heart ischemia (chest pressure/tightness, exertional pain, or pain relieved by rest) rather than primarily lung symptoms?

Yes, it feels like chest pain/tightness on the left side and upper chest, and it radiates to my left arm and scapula. I’m not sure about exertional triggers because I’ve mainly been feeling it even at rest, but it is definitely heart-ischemia-like in how it feels.
[ASK] Do you have chest pain/pressure that is new, worsening, or occurs at rest and lasts more than 10 minutes?
Yes. It’s new and worsening, and it happens at rest. It has lasted more than 10 minutes.
